title: CurvePrimitiveBezierNode — create bezier curve segments
description: Implement a curve_bezier DSL node equivalent to Blender's GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveBezierSegment. Creates a cubic Bezier curve from start point, start handle, end handle, and end point. This is the foundational curve primitive — all armor cross-sections and rail curves in Blender-Procedural-Human are defined with Bezier segments. Without this, agents cannot create arbitrary smooth curves for lofting, sweeping, or profile definition. Should also support a quadratic variant (3 control points) as a mode parameter.
definition-of-done:
1. New CurvePrimitiveBezierNode class in ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/nodes/curve/ with @MeshNodeAnnotation id 'curve_bezier'
2. Input ports: start (Vec3Field), handle_start (Vec3Field), handle_end (Vec3Field), end (Vec3Field), resolution (IntField, default=16), mode (StringField: 'CUBIC' or 'QUADRATIC', default='CUBIC')
3. Output port: curve (GeometryBundleValue) — polyline approximation of the Bezier curve
4. CUBIC mode: standard cubic Bezier with 4 control points
5. QUADRATIC mode: quadratic Bezier with 3 control points (start, handle_start as single control, end)
6. Resolution controls how many line segments approximate the curve
7. Output curve is compatible with existing curve nodes (resample_curve, curve_sweep, mesh_to_curve)
8. Registered in MeshNodeRegistry and usable in .dsl files
testing-plan:
1. Unit test: straight line bezier (handles on line) — verify points are collinear
2. Unit test: semicircle bezier — verify approximate circular arc within tolerance
3. Unit test: quadratic mode with 3 points — verify correct interpolation
4. Unit test: resolution parameter — verify output point count matches resolution+1
5. DSL integration: create bezier curve, pipe through curve_sweep — verify smooth tube
6. Mesh probe: verify bounding box encompasses all control points
